Data source overview  
The provided “paper” is only a bibliography list (nine citation entries published 1988-1993).  It contains no narrative text, no section titles, no description of risks, problems, methods, findings, or interventions.  Because there is no substantive content, no causal-interventional reasoning pathways can be reconstructed.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[12]  
The output adheres to the requested format, but confidence is very low because no knowledge fabric can be recovered from a purely bibliographic list.

Inference strategy justification  
• I scanned every citation for possible implicit content; none supplies any explanatory prose.  
• Creating nodes by guessing at the content of the cited works would violate the requirement to stay within the data source or, if inferred, to mark everything as speculative.  That would yield an entirely speculative graph with confidence 1, which would be misleading.  
• Therefore the only faithful approach is to report that extraction is not possible.

Extraction completeness explanation  
All available information (authors, titles, venues) was considered.  No explicit or implicit causal reasoning or interventions appear, hence the node/edge lists are empty by design and the mandatory verification checklist cannot be satisfied.

Key limitations  
1. Bibliography-only sources provide no material for fabric construction.  
2. Without titles’ full text, we cannot safely infer concrete risks, problem analyses, or interventions.  
3. The current instruction set presumes some explanatory prose; a fallback policy for bibliography-only inputs would help.

JSON output
```json
{
  "nodes": [],
  "edges": []
}
```

How to improve the instruction set  
1. Include a branch in the pipeline that detects “bibliography-only” or “non-textual” inputs early, skipping extraction and flagging the source for manual follow-up.  
2. Allow a “no-extraction-possible” flag in the JSON so downstream systems can handle such cases gracefully.  
3. Provide explicit guidance on whether title-only inference is encouraged or discouraged and how to mark confidence appropriately.
